targetText: In this conflict between national duty and class interest, the Government of National Defence did not hesitate one moment to turn into a Government of National Defection
summary: National defense subordinated to class defense: the ruling class feared armed workers more than foreign invaders.
explanation: Marx demonstrates that bourgeois leaders prefer military defeat by a foreign enemy over the victory of an armed working class that threatens capitalist property relations.

targetText: Trochu's "plan" was known to his colleagues to be the capitulation of Paris
summary: The capitulationist deception: Trochu's plan was from the beginning to starve and disarm Paris into surrender.
explanation: Marx exposes that the Government of National Defense feigned patriotism while secretly arranging Paris's capitulation to crush working-class revolutionary mobilization.

targetText: Theirs, that monstrous gnome, has charmed the French bourgeoisie for almost half a century, because he is the most consummate intellectual expression of their own class corruption
summary: Adolphe Thiers as the embodiment of bourgeois corruption: a political mercenary devoted to defending capital.
explanation: Marx presents a scathing historical profile of Adolphe Thiers, detailing his decades of political betrayals, financial graft, and ruthless suppression of working-class uprisings.

targetText: armed working men of Paris were the only serious obstacle in the way of counter-revolutionary conspiracy
summary: The armed proletariat as the sole barrier to reaction: capitalist politicians conspired to disarm Paris to force a royalist restoration.
explanation: The Paris National Guard, composed of armed workers, stood as the only force capable of defending republican liberties against the monarchist Assembly at Versailles.

targetText: conflict between the Paris of the working class and the National Assembly
summary: Class conflict between red Paris and the rural landlord Assembly: Paris represented revolution while Versailles represented feudal and capitalist reaction.
explanation: Marx contrasts the revolutionary proletarian consciousness of Paris with the reactionary Assembly of 'rurals' (landlords and monarchists) assembled at Bordeaux and Versailles.

targetText: disarming of Paris was decreed as an imperious necessity
summary: The necessity of disarming Paris: Thiers was forced to attack the National Guard to secure bourgeois state power.
explanation: To enforce Prussian war indemnities and secure capitalist domination, Thiers had to disarm the Paris workers, setting the stage for the March 18 revolution.
